# HydroModPy

> HydroModPy computes where groundwater comes out of the ground and which streams it keeps alive, month by month, for a whole catchment. These are its documentation pages. Each line links to a page; llms-full.txt holds the text of all of them.

## Home

- [HydroModPy](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/index.html): A Python toolbox for automated, reproducible, catchment-scale modelling of shallow groundwater.

## Understand

- [Understand HydroModPy](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/index.html): HydroModPy simulates the groundwater of a catchment from its relief, its geology and its rainfall.
- [Can I check what was run?](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/can-i-check-what-was-run.html): Yes. A result of HydroModPy is not only a map.
- [Glossary](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/glossary.html): The terms used in this part of the site, with a short definition.
- [How sure is the model?](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/how-sure.html): Not completely, and no groundwater model is.
- [In five minutes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/in-five-minutes.html): One map, five sentences. If you read nothing else, read this page.
- [Scoring a simulated stream network](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/network-metrics.html): A model makes a network of streams. A map draws another one.
- [Reading the results](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/reading-results.html): This page is a reading guide to the main outputs of example 04 (the Nançon catchment, see Understand HydroModPy).
- [How the model makes streams](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/stream-network.html): HydroModPy does not draw rivers. It computes a water table.
- [What the model computes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/what-it-computes.html): HydroModPy solves the flow of water in the saturated part of the ground of a catchment, the part that lies below the water table.
- [What “validated” means here](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/what-validated-means.html): The word validated is used loosely. In this documentation it has a narrow meaning.
- [Where the data come from](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/understand/where-the-data-come-from.html): A result is only as good as its inputs. This page names the data that HydroModPy can read, who produces them, how fine they are, and what to do about their licences.

## Get started

- [Get started](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/index.html): Install HydroModPy, run a first model in under a minute, then climb example 04 in six files.
- [The staircase](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/staircase/index.html): Example 04 models the Nançon catchment (Ille-et-Vilaine) with MODFLOW 6.
- [Concepts](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/concepts.html): Four words name the things on disk. This page is the whole mental model you need before the staircase.
- [Install](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/install.html): HydroModPy needs Python 3.11, 3.12 or 3.13.
- [After the staircase](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/staircase/next.html): You ran the six steps, or enough of them.
- [Step 1: the shortest file that runs](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/staircase/step1.html): Solve the Nançon catchment in steady state from one short file.
- [Step 2: the mapped network and the gauge](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/staircase/step2.html): Compare the cells where the simulated water table reaches the surface with the mapped river network and the gauge.
- [Step 3: the same data, from the APIs](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/staircase/step3.html): Fetch the river network and the gauge from the BD Topage and Hub’Eau APIs instead of local files.
- [Step 4: the transient run](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/staircase/step4.html): Run the model month by month over 2000-2002 and see which cells flow, and for how long.
- [Step 5: every export](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/staircase/step5.html): Write the results of step 4 in every format HydroModPy can export, and ask for more files once the run exists.
- [Step 6: the soil reservoir](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/get-started/staircase/step6.html): Compute the recharge from the rain and the evapotranspiration instead of reading it, and run the model every day over 2015-2020.

## Reference

- [Command line](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/index.html): $ hmp [-h] [-V] <command> ...
- [Reference](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/index.html)
- [`[analysis]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/analysis/index.html): Hub aggregating every post-simulation analysis sub-section.
- [`[calibration]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/index.html): Top-level `[calibration]` section.
- [`[data]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/index.html): Top-level `[data]` configuration for manager families.
- [`[flow]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/index.html): Flow-process configuration.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/index.html): Top-level container for all sink/source elements of the flow process.
- [TOML parameters](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/index.html): Every section of the configuration file, generated from the models.
- [`[site_selection]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/index.html): Top-level site-selection workflow configuration.
- [`hmp.index()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-index.html): Found in the code
- [Python API](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/index.html): import hydromodpy as hmp
- [Calibration methods and metrics](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/calibration-methods.html): Every search method a calibration file can name, and every metric an objective block can score with.
- [What changed in the TOML](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/changes.html): Fields added, renamed, removed or changed between two versions.
- [`hmp audit`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/audit.html): $ hmp audit [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp calibrate`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/calibrate.html): Uses hmp.calibrate().
- [`hmp catalog`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/catalog.html): $ hmp catalog [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp config`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/config.html): $ hmp config [-h] {template,check,resolve,schema,targets,wizard} ...
- [`hmp data`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/data.html): $ hmp data [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp dev`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/dev.html): Uses hmp.example_add(), hmp.example_list(), hmp.example_show().
- [`hmp doctor`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/doctor.html): $ hmp doctor [-h] [--workspace WORKSPACE] [--toml TOML] [--json] [--cross-catalog] [--lifecycle] [--prt] [--fix-config FILE.toml] [--migrate]
- [`hmp example`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/example.html): Uses hmp.example_add(), hmp.example_list(), hmp.example_show().
- [Exit codes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/exit-codes.html): A command ends with the code of its outcome.
- [`hmp export`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/export.html): Uses hmp.open(), hmp.export().
- [`hmp install-binaries`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/install-binaries.html): $ hmp install-binaries [-h] [--subset SUBSET] [--mf6-prt] [--bindir BINDIR] [--release RELEASE] [--upgrade] [--quiet]
- [`hmp privacy`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/privacy.html): $ hmp privacy [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp process`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/process.html): $ hmp process [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp project`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/project.html): $ hmp project [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp report`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/report.html): Uses hmp.compare_pair(), hmp.report().
- [`hmp run`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/run.html): Uses hmp.run().
- [`hmp site-selection`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/site-selection.html): $ hmp site-selection [-h] {plan,select-catchments,build-observed,build-generated,report} ...
- [`hmp spinup`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/spinup.html): Uses hmp.spinup().
- [`hmp test`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/test.html): $ hmp test [-h] [--list] [--fast] [--slow] [--extensive] [--nwt] [--mf6] [--intercomparison] [--steady] [--transient] [--analytical] [--short] [--update-goldens] [-j JOBS]...
- [`hmp viz`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/viz.html): $ hmp viz [-h] <action> ...
- [`hmp workspace`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/cli/workspace.html): $ hmp workspace [-h] <action> ...
- [Data sources](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/data-sources.html): Every data section of the file, and the sources its `source` key accepts, with who publishes each one and under which licence.
- [Figures](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/figures.html): Every figure HydroModPy can draw, read from the figure registry of the code: what it reads, when it can be drawn, the options it takes with their type and default, and the class that draws it.
- [`[analysis.batch]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/analysis/batch.html): Validated top-level configuration for one regional-lab run.
- [`[analysis.capability_gallery]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/analysis/capability_gallery.html): Optional publication target for stable, versionable run figures.
- [`[analysis.comparison]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/analysis/comparison.html): Top-level comparison experiment section.
- [Calibrable parameters](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibrable.html): A calibration moves the keys below. Name one in `calibration.parameters.<name>.path` and give its range in `calibration.parameters.<name>.bounds`, in the unit the key declares.
- [`[calibration.aggregate]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/aggregate.html): How several scored targets become one cost.
- [`[[calibration.objective_blocks]]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/objective_blocks.html): Weighted metric block used by a composite objective.
- [`[calibration.outputs]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/outputs.html): Named observables extracted from each candidate run.
- [`[calibration.parameters]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/parameters.html): User declaration for one calibrated parameter.
- [`[calibration.persistence]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/persistence.html): Orthogonal switch governing every persistence sink.
- [`[[calibration.phases]]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/phases.html): One stage of a calibration that runs in several.
- [`[calibration.protocol]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/protocol.html): What a file may say about the protocol beyond naming it.
- [`[calibration.scoring_window]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/scoring_window.html): Dates bounding the samples a metric is computed on.
- [`[calibration.uncertainty]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/calibration/uncertainty.html): How wide the search says its own answer is.
- [`[data.crossings]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/crossings.html): Top-level crossings variable configuration.
- [`[data.dem]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/dem.html): Top-level DEM variable configuration.
- [`[data.etp]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/etp.html): Top-level potential evapotranspiration configuration.
- [`[data.geology]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/geology.html): Top-level geology variable configuration.
- [`[data.humidity]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/humidity.html): Top-level relative-humidity configuration.
- [`[data.hydrography]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/hydrography.html): Top-level hydrography configuration.
- [`[data.hydrometry]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/hydrometry.html): Top-level hydrometry configuration.
- [`[data.intermittency]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/intermittency.html): Top-level intermittency configuration.

- [`[data.oceanic]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/oceanic.html): Top-level oceanic configuration.

- [`[data.soil_capacity]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/soil_capacity.html): Soil available water capacity raster, read by the soil reservoir.
- [`[data.soil_moisture]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/soil_moisture.html): Top-level soil-moisture configuration.

- [`[data.water_quality]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/water_quality.html): Top-level water quality configuration.
- [`[data.wind]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/data/wind.html): Top-level wind-speed configuration.
- [`[display]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/display.html): Display behaviour resolved from the `[display]` TOML section.
- [`[domain]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/domain.html): Domain configuration.
- [`[[export]]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/export.html): One export: what to write, when, in which format, where.
- [`[flow.bc]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/bc.html): Mapping of flow boundary-condition payloads parsed from `[flow.bc]`.
- [`[flow.ic]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/ic.html): Container for flow initial conditions stored in process runtime.
- [`[flow.param]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/param.html): Flow parameter payload using native field-param sections.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.etp]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/etp.html): Typed payload for diffuse evapotranspiration over the model domain.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.flow_barriers]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/flow_barriers.html): Typed payload for one MODFLOW 6 horizontal flow barrier (HFB).
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.lakes]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/lakes.html): Typed boundary-condition payload for one MODFLOW 6 LAK lake.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.recharge]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/recharge.html): Typed payload for diffuse recharge over the model domain.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.sfr]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/sfr.html): Typed boundary-condition payload for one MODFLOW 6 SFR stream network.
- [`[flow.sinks_sources.wells]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/flow/sinks_sources/wells.html): Typed payload for one pumping or injection well.
- [`[geographic]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/geographic.html): Geographic configuration for watershed delineation.
- [The grammar of a HydroModPy file](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/grammar.html): One TOML file describes a run. Its sections are listed in TOML parameters; this page gives the rules they all share: tables, inheritance, quantities, dates, paths, free keys and profiles.
- [`[hydrometry]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/hydrometry.html): Top-level hydrometry configuration.
- [`[mesh_catchment]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/mesh_catchment.html): Top-level launcher contract for one mono-catchment meshing run.
- [`[mesh_input]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/mesh_input.html): External pre-existing mesh declared in `[mesh_input]`.
- [Minimal files](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/minimal-files.html): For each section, the smallest file that holds it: the sections every file needs, then the keys the section requires, each with its example value or its default.
- [`[modflow6]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/modflow6.html): Expert-level MODFLOW 6 configuration organized by concern.
- [`[modflownwt]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/modflownwt.html): Expert-level MODFLOW configuration organized by concern.
- [`[observation]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/observation.html): Configuration for `[observation]`: points sampled during the run.
- [`[overview]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/overview.html): Overview report settings (watershed identity card).
- [Find a key by what it measures](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/quantities.html): Every user key whose unit or form the code declares, grouped by kind of quantity.
- [The catchment report file](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/report-file.html): The catchment report file read by `hmp report catchment`.
- [`[simulation]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/simulation.html): Minimal orchestration block declared under `[simulation]`.
- [`[site_selection.criteria]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/criteria.html): Criteria of the selection, one table per family.
- [`[site_selection.dem]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/dem.html): DEM source requested by site selection.
- [`[site_selection.dem_area_light]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/dem_area_light.html): Minimal DEM-only basin selection settings.
- [`[site_selection.hydrology]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/hydrology.html): DEM-derived hydrologic products requested by the selection workflow.
- [`[site_selection.input]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/input.html): Execution input selector used by the `site_selection` workflow.
- [`[site_selection.map_context]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/map_context.html): Optional static context layers for review figures.
- [`[site_selection.outlets]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/outlets.html): Candidate outlet generation settings.
- [`[site_selection.output]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/output.html): Output artifact switches.
- [`[site_selection.spatial_selection]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/spatial_selection.html): Spatial thinning and overlap policy.
- [`[site_selection.strategy]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/strategy.html): High-level strategy controlling candidate generation and criterion order.
- [`[site_selection.territory]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/site_selection/territory.html): Spatial domain where candidate basins are searched.
- [`[solver]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/solver.html): Configuration block defining the active groundwater solver engine.
- [`[spinup]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/spinup.html): Settings for the cyclic spin-up loop (`[spinup]`).
- [`[testbed]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/testbed.html): Validated configuration for one method testbed.
- [`[transport]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/transport.html): Transport-process configuration.
- [`[workflow]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/workflow.html): Workflow selector configuration.
- [`[workspace]`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/parameters/workspace.html): Strict-binary workspace configuration.

- [`hmp.export()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-export.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.figure()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-figure.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.open()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-open.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.read()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-read.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.report()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-report.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.run()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-run.html): Found in the code
- [`hmp.spinup()`](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/hmp-spinup.html): Found in the code
- [Objects and how they relate](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/python/objects.html): A run is a folder on disk: field arrays in Zarr, tables in Parquet, under `<project>/runs/<name>/`.
- [Solvers](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/reference/solvers.html): Every process a run can plan and the solver that carries it out, read from the solver registry of the code: what each pair provides, the lines of the TOML file that select it, the executable it runs,...

## Theory

- [Theory](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/index.html): Theory covers what HydroModPy computes or decides: the rules it applies when it builds a model, the conversions from TOML to solver input, the methods it implements itself, and what it refuses.
- [Bibliography](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/bibliography.html): References cited in the HydroModPy documentation.
- [Boussinesq theory](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/boussinesq.html): This page gives the equations of the in-house Boussinesq solver, in the order the code applies them, with what they assume and where they stop being true.
- [The inverse problem of a calibration](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/calibration/inverse-problem-formulation.html): A calibration turns a question about the site, such as “which conductivity makes the model reproduce the gauge and the mapped streams?”, into the search for the minimum, or the root, of one number...
- [Downslope distance between two networks](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/downslope-distance.html): A mapped stream network and a simulated one rarely coincide.
- [How water leaves the aquifer](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits.html): Water enters the saturated zone as recharge and leaves it through a few exits.
- [Drains and evapotranspiration at the top of the model](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/drains-and-et.html): Two exits act at the top of the model. A drain discharges where the water table reaches the ground.
- [Fixed heads: the sea, the rivers and the sides](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/head-boundaries.html): A fixed head takes the head of a cell out of the solution.
- [Lakes and reservoirs](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/lakes.html): A lake is a boundary package laid on the aquifer grid.
- [Routing on the mesh: the descent D](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/routing-on-the-mesh.html): Where the water of a drain goes next is a question of routing.
- [Where the water table reaches the surface](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/simulated-network.html): The model produces sources, not a stream network.
- [Streams and the water mover](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/exits/streams-and-mover.html): A stream network (SFR) routes the water it receives from reach to reach and exchanges water with the aquifer through its bed.
- [Rain and evaporation: the forcing](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/forcing.html): The aquifer model does not see days: it sees stress periods, and one rate per cell for each period.
- [The groundwater flow problem](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/groundwater-flow.html): What head does the aquifer hold, in every cell and at every time?
- [The mesh](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/mesh.html): The solver does not see the DEM. It sees cells, and one top elevation, one bottom elevation and one centre for each of them.
- [Notation](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/notation.html): Every symbol of the theory pages, with its unit and the key that sets it.
- [The daily soil reservoir](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/soil-reservoir.html): Each day, a soil store takes the rain, loses water to evapotranspiration, and sends the water it cannot hold down to the water table.
- [The solvers of the aquifer](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/solvers.html): HydroModPy integrates the groundwater flow equation with one of three solvers: MODFLOW 6, MODFLOW-NWT or the in-house Boussinesq solver.
- [From a zone map to the cells](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/solvers/field-to-cell-parameter-transfer.html): A property such as \(K\) is given per zone of a map: geology classes, bands, rings, or the zones of a raster.
- [XT3D on irregular meshes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/solvers/xt3d-on-irregular-disv-meshes.html): The two-point flux of (17) is exact on a grid whose connections are perpendicular to the faces, for a conductivity that is the same in every horizontal direction.
- [Time alignment of outputs and observations](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/time-alignment.html): A run writes one value per stress period.
- [Validation](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/theory/validation.html): Each check below is a test of `tests/validation/`.

## About

- [About](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/index.html): Who builds HydroModPy, how to cite it, where it is used and which version to install.
- [Applications and papers](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/applications.html): Studies that used HydroModPy, newest first.
- [Changelog](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/changelog.html): Every release of HydroModPy and every change since the last one, newest first.
- [Cite](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/cite.html): If HydroModPy supports your work, cite the technical note.
- [Versions and stability](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/versions.html): This site documents version 2.0.0a5. It is a pre-release of the 2.0 line.
- [Work with us](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/about/work-with-us.html): HydroModPy is open research software under the EPL-2.0 licence.

## Optional

- [Calibration architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/calibration/index.html): Software architecture of the calibration stack in `hydromodpy.calibration`: the code-oriented architecture map plus the full operational guide for adding methods, observables, and objectives.
- [Data loading architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/data_loading/index.html): The data layer is the orchestration boundary for data loading.
- [Field layer](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/field/index.html): This section documents the `hydromodpy.spatial.field` layer.
- [Recipes](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/index.html): Each recipe answers “I want to add X: where does it go and what contract must I honour?”.
- [Architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/index.html): How the code is organised: the layers and their allowed imports, the packages, the storage layout and the subsystems.
- [Mesh architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/mesh/index.html): How HydroModPy turns a watershed support into a solver-ready mesh: the catchment-conformal Gmsh pipeline, the structured-grid path used by MODFLOW-family solvers, and the cross-mesh pivot format...
- [Packages](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/index.html): One page per top-level subpackage of `hydromodpy/`.
- [Spatial support and hydrography](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/spatial_support/index.html): How HydroModPy defines spatial zones and supports, how they are consumed by `Field` and `FieldParam` during heterogeneous parameter mapping, and how hydrography drives stream supports and simulated...
- [Documentation](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/documentation/index.html): This site is built from the code as much as the code allows.
- [Contribute](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/index.html): This part is for people who change HydroModPy itself.
- [Project](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/project/index.html): How the project is checked, tested and released, and where it is going.
- [Calibration architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/calibration/calibration-architecture.html): This page is the code-oriented entry point for the calibration stack: the package map, the reading path, the loop of one session and the core classes.
- [How the calibration engine runs](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/calibration/calibration-guide.html): This page is for a contributor who changes the calibration code in `hydromodpy/calibration/`.
- [Contracts and design patterns](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/contracts.html): This page lists what users and integrators can rely on (the public facade, two storage Protocols, the field registry), then the patterns the code reuses.
- [Data scopes and schema evolution](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/data-scopes.html): HydroModPy splits SQL state across three scopes: machine, workspace, project.
- [CI workflows](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/ci.html): Built from `.github/workflows/*.yml` each time the site is built.
- [Environment variables](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/environment.html): Built from `hydromodpy/core/env.py`; the files that read each variable come from a scan of the code each time the site is built.
- [Optional dependencies](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/extras.html): Built from `[project.optional-dependencies]` of `pyproject.toml` each time the site is built.
- [Architecture gates](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/guards.html): Built from the module docstrings of `tests/unit/architecture/test_*.py` and the YAML contracts beside them each time the site is built.
- [Layer graph](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/layers.html): Built from `tests/unit/architecture/layer_matrix.yaml` each time the site is built.
- [Packages and registries](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/packages.html): Built from the registries of the code and the folders of `hydromodpy/` each time the site is built.
- [Storage tree](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/storage-tree.html): Built from `hydromodpy/results/storage/contract.py`, `hydromodpy/core/state/paths.py` and `hydromodpy/schema/generated_views.py` each time the site is built.
- [Test inventory](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/generated/tests.html): Built from the test files of `tests/`, read without running them, and `pytest.ini` each time the site is built.
- [Add a block HTML report](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-block-html-report.html): Use this recipe when a workflow must emit a static HTML report composed of reusable blocks: metrics, figures, tables, artifact links, and warnings.
- [Add a calibration method](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-calibration-method.html): Calibration in HydroModPy runs an ask/tell loop: an optimizer proposes a parameter point, the engine evaluates it, the optimizer ingests the result.
- [Add a CLI command](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-cli-command.html): The `hmp` and `hydromodpy` CLIs share the same dispatcher in `hydromodpy/cli/main.py`.
- [Add a config field](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-config-field.html): Every TOML knob in HydroModPy is backed by a Pydantic v2 model that forbids extra keys.
- [Add a data source](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-data-source.html): A source is one value a user may write in `source =` for an existing variable: a public API, the user’s own files (`custom`), or a generator (`constant`, `synthetic`).
- [Add a data variable](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-data-variable.html): A data variable is one `[data.<name>]` section of a project TOML, loaded by one manager and stored in the input cache.
- [Add a figure](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-figure.html): Figures live in `hydromodpy.display` and are auto-discovered through `display/figures/__init__.py` (`pkgutil.iter_modules`).
- [Add a process](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-process.html): A process is a runtime payload that one or more solver adapters consume.
- [Add a solver](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-solver.html): A solver in HydroModPy is one `(process_type, solver_name)` pair bound to a concrete backend.
- [Add a test](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-a-test.html): The test tree under `tests/` has one folder per family.
- [Add an exporter](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/add-an-exporter.html): Exporters convert simulation results into external file formats.
- [Build a frontend](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/build-a-frontend.html): HydroModPy is a Python library. It ships no HTTP server, no FastAPI binding and no websocket.
- [Cut a release](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/cut-a-release.html): A release is a Git tag. The tag starts three jobs: the publication to PyPI, the GitHub Release, and the build of the documentation for that version.
- [Fix a failing architecture gate](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/how-to/fix-an-architecture-gate.html): python -m pytest tests/unit/architecture -q -n 2
- [Layered architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/layered-architecture.html): HydroModPy is a layered dependency graph.
- [Mental model and design choices](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/mental-model.html): This page explains why HydroModPy is split into several layers instead of collapsing everything into one execution object.
- [Catchment mesh architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/mesh/catchment-mesh-architecture.html): This page documents the dedicated catchment-mesh workflow built around `hydromodpy.spatial.mesh`: package layout, runtime entry points, batch loop, simulation embedding, output layout, and the...
- [Conformal Gmsh meshing](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/mesh/gmsh-meshing.html): Architecture note: three concepts cooperate to produce a 2D mesh that conforms to geological zones and the hydrographic network.
- [The HydroMesh pivot](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/mesh/mesh-pivot.html): HydroModPy manipulates several 2D and 3D mesh types to discretize hydrogeological parameters (conductivity, storage, recharge) and to pass them to the solvers.
- [Structured grid architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/mesh/structured-grid-architecture.html): This page documents the FloPy `StructuredGrid` path used by the MODFLOW-family solvers: static object model, build sequence, and the bridge to `Field` / `FieldParam` for solver-ready arrays.
- [Package: analysis](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/analysis.html): Workflows that work across runs. `analysis` compares simulations that share a case, runs a matrix of controlled variants of a method, and publishes selected figures of a run to a gallery folder.
- [Package: calibration](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/calibration.html): Fitting model parameters to observations.
- [Package: catalog](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/catalog.html): A read-only view over the input cache of a workspace.
- [Package: cli](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/cli.html): The command line: the `hmp` and `hydromodpy` entry points.
- [Package: config](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/config.html): The root of the configuration. `HydroModPyConfig` is the one Pydantic model that aggregates every section of a project TOML.
- [Package: core](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/core.html): The kernel leaf. Every other layer may import `core`, and `core` imports no sibling layer, not even under `TYPE_CHECKING`.
- [Package: data](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/data.html): Everything a run reads from outside: provider APIs, user files, their cache and the typed records handed to the layers above.
- [Package: display](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/display.html): It holds three things of unequal weight:
- [Package: examples](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/examples.html): What `hmp example` stands on: the catalog of shipped examples, the cache their files are fetched into, and the generator that writes the catalog from a checkout.
- [Package: physics](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/physics.html): The physical processes of a model, written without any solver.
- [Package: project](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/project.html): A project driven from Python: one object, `Project`, that holds a validated configuration, builds the model once, and runs it as often as asked.
- [Package: reporting](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/reporting.html): Standalone HTML pages that put several results side by side.
- [Package: results](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/results.html): What a run leaves on disk, and how it is read back.
- [Package: schema](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/schema.html): The contracts that something outside the Python code relies on.
- [Package: simulation](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/simulation.html): From the `[simulation]` table to a solved run and the outputs read back from it.
- [Package: solver](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/solver.html): The numerical backends. A `[solver]` table picks the flow backend, and a `[[simulation.process]]` entry names the solvers each process runs.
- [Package: spatial](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/spatial.html): Where the model is in space.
- [Package: validity_frame](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/validity_frame.html): It is outside the stable V1 public API and has no compatibility guarantee.
- [Package: workflow](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/packages/workflow.html): The order in which a project is built and run.
- [Pipeline resume from artefacts](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/pipeline_resume.html): The simulation pipeline rebuilds its in-memory state exclusively from durable artefacts and the TOML config.
- [Flow boundary conditions](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/process/flow-boundary-conditions.html): This page documents the runtime contract used for groundwater flow boundary conditions.
- [Process architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/process/process-architecture.html): This page is the code-oriented entry point for `hydromodpy.physics`, the layer that turns validated configuration into the runtime `Flow` and `Transport` objects consumed by solver adapters.
- [Comparison workflow architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/simulation/comparison-workflow.html): This page documents the contract of `[workflow].mode = "comparison"`.
- [Testbed workflow architecture](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/simulation/testbed-workflow-architecture.html): The key design rule is:
- [From TOML to solver outputs](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/simulation/toml-to-solver-walkthrough.html): A code-oriented walkthrough of the main execution chain, from one TOML file to the solver outputs and the stored run.
- [MODFLOW and Boussinesq backends](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/solver/backends.html): How the three flow backends are put together, what they share, and the contracts the MODFLOW family honours.
- [Boussinesq engines and experimental closures](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/solver/boussinesq-engines.html): The equations of the Boussinesq solver are on Boussinesq theory.
- [Boussinesq solver diagrams](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/solver/boussinesq-uml-diagrams.html): These diagrams document the software architecture of `hydromodpy.solver.boussinesq`.
- [Simulated active network](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/spatial_support/hydrographic-network-simulated-active-inventory.html): What HydroModPy computes for the network that emerges from simulated flow, and what it does not store.
- [Hydrographic network diagrams](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/spatial_support/hydrographic-network-uml-diagrams.html): These diagrams document the software architecture around the hydrographic network concept introduced to unify:
- [Spatial support diagrams](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/spatial_support/spatial-support-uml-diagrams.html): These diagrams document the architecture around:
- [Choosing a spatial support](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/spatial_support/support-selection-guide.html): This page complements the UML diagrams with a simple question: which support type should be used for a given heterogeneous parameterization?
- [Storage layout](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/architecture/storage-layout.html): Disk is the truth. The database is an index rebuilt from disk.
- [Docstring policy](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/docstring-policy.html): The Python API reference is generated from the code.
- [Documentation coverage](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/documentation/coverage.html): What the models leave undocumented, computed at each build from the field registry.
- [How the docs are built](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/documentation/how-the-docs-are-built.html): The site is a Sphinx 9 project in `docs/source/`, with the PyData theme 0.23 and MyST 5.1.
- [Contributor handbook](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/handbook.html): How to report a problem, set up a development environment, follow the coding style, run the tests and send a change.
- [Reading a failing check](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/project/ci-workflows.html): HydroModPy has one pull-request gate and a set of focused workflows under `.github/workflows/`.
- [V1 release contract](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/project/release-contract-v1.html): This page records the stable V1 surface and the intentional exclusions.
- [Tests](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/project/tests.html): HydroModPy splits tests into families because they answer different questions.
- [Quick start](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/quick-start.html): Ten minutes from a clone to a first commit.
- [Roadmap](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/roadmap.html): The issue tracker is the live source of truth for work in flight.
- [Write a theory page](https://docs.hydromodpy.fr/dev/contribute/write-a-theory-page.html): A theory page gives the equations of one model, in the order the code applies them, with their assumptions and their limits.
